subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve distinct ACP child-session parallelism and require live root-cause proof before changing it, or intentionally add a narrower concurrency gate for ACP/Claude spawns?
rationale: Current source and tests preserve parallel distinct ACP sessions, while the report suggests a launch-readiness race that needs live ACPX/Claude proof before changing concurrency semantics.

options.title: Preserve parallelism and prove root cause
options.body: Keep this issue open for a live two-spawn ACPX/Claude smoke and fix the confirmed launch-readiness boundary without broad serialization.

options.title: Add a concurrency gate
options.body: Intentionally serialize or limit ACP/Claude child launches if maintainers accept slower delegated work to avoid backend races.

options.title: Close after clean live smoke
options.body: Close only if a current latest-release or main smoke shows both rapid child sessions launch and produce output reliably.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism and prove root cause
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a live two-spawn ACPX/Claude smoke and fix the confirmed launch-readiness boundary without broad serialization.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP manager and ACPX startup ownership makes this the best available routing candidate for the concurrency-versus-launch-readiness choice.
